legend: Evlampiy was gifted a rooted tree. The vertices of the tree are numbered from 1%%ZSMJ0%% to n%%ZSMJ1%%. Each of its vertices also has an integer ai%%ZSMJ2%% written on it. For each vertex i%%ZSMJ3%%, Evlampiy calculated ci%%ZSMJ4%% — the number of vertices j%%ZSMJ5%% in the subtree of vertex i%%ZSMJ6%%, such that aj<ai%%ZSMJ7%%.

After the new year, Evlampiy could not remember what his gift was! He remembers the tree and the values of ci%%ZSMJ10%%, but he completely forgot which integers ai%%ZSMJ11%% were written on the vertices.
Help him to restore initial integers!
input: The first line contains an integer n%%ZSMJ12%% (1≤n≤2000)%%ZSMJ13%% — the number of vertices in the tree.

The next n%%ZSMJ14%% lines contain descriptions of vertices: the i%%ZSMJ15%%-th line contains two integers pi%%ZSMJ16%% and ci%%ZSMJ17%% (0≤pi≤n%%ZSMJ18%%; 0≤ci≤n−1%%ZSMJ19%%), where pi%%ZSMJ20%% is the parent of vertex i%%ZSMJ21%% or 0%%ZSMJ22%% if vertex i%%ZSMJ23%% is root, and ci%%ZSMJ24%% is the number of vertices j%%ZSMJ25%% in the subtree of vertex i%%ZSMJ26%%, such that aj<ai%%ZSMJ27%%.
It is guaranteed that the values of pi%%ZSMJ28%% describe a rooted tree with n%%ZSMJ29%% vertices.
output: If a solution exists, in the first line print "YES", and in the second line output n%%ZSMJ30%% integers ai%%ZSMJ31%% (1≤ai≤109)%%ZSMJ32%%. If there are several solutions, output any of them. One can prove that if there is a solution, then there is also a solution in which all ai%%ZSMJ33%% are between 1%%ZSMJ34%% and 109%%ZSMJ35%%.
If there are no solutions, print "NO".
